en.title: Relative clauses
en.summary: A relative clause adds information about a noun.

paragraphs: A relative clause follows a noun and gives more information about it. It begins with a relative pronoun (who, whom, which, that, whose) or with where, when or why.

items: The woman **who lives next door** is a doctor.
This is the book **that I bought**.
That is the town **where I was born**.

blocks.html:
WordUsed forExample
whopeopleThe man who called is here.
whichthingsThe car which broke down is old.
thatpeople or thingsThe film that we saw was long.
whosepossessionThe girl whose bag was lost cried.
whereplacesthe café where we met
whentimesthe day when I arrived
whyreasonsthe reason why he left

paragraphs: A defining clause is necessary to identify the noun, and it is not separated by commas. A non-defining clause adds extra information, is separated by commas, and cannot use that.

blocks.html:
DefiningNon-defining
The man who called is my uncle.My uncle, who lives in Leeds, called.
The house that I like is old.The house, which is old, is for sale.

paragraphs: In a defining clause, you can leave out who, which or that when it is the object of the clause: The book I bought was good. You cannot leave it out when it is the subject.

blocks.html:
Object (can be left out)Subject (cannot be left out)
The film (that) we saw was long.The film that won the prize was long.
The man (whom) I met was kind.The man who met me was kind.

items: Wrong: **The man which called is here.** Right: **who called**
Wrong: **The book that I bought it is good.** Right: **The book that I bought is good.**
Wrong: **My sister, that lives in Rome,...** Right: **My sister, who lives in Rome,...**
